modes.cue_notes: Sit with both legs extended forward. Allow the spine to round into a C-curve as you fold forward over the legs — do not attempt to keep the back flat. Let the head hang, arms rest on legs or floor. The pelvis will tuck and the posterior spinal ligaments will receive the primary stress. Focus on relaxing any muscular holding and allowing gravity to deepen the pose over time.

source: Traditional yin yoga; see Paul Grilley, Bernie Clark, Sarah Powers
notes: The yin version intentionally rounds the spine to compress the posterior discs and stretch the spinal ligaments. Kidney and bladder meridians run the entire back line from heel to occiput.

breathing_cues.entering: Inhale to elongate the spine, then on a long exhale, allow the whole back body to round forward — pelvis tilting back, spine curling, head releasing last. Do not hold yourself up.
breathing_cues.holding: Breathe into the back body. Imagine the inhale expanding the space between the shoulder blades; on the exhale, surrender a little deeper into the fold. Let muscular effort dissolve with every breath cycle.
breathing_cues.exiting: On an inhale, press the hands into the floor beside the hips and slowly roll the spine upright, one vertebra at a time, letting the head come up last.

modifications.name: Bolster Across Thighs
modifications.description: Lay a bolster across the thighs and rest the torso on it, allowing complete passive surrender of the back body without any active holding.

modifications.name: Bent Knees Variation
modifications.description: Keep a generous bend in the knees so that the pelvis can tip forward naturally, reducing strain on the posterior knee and allowing the spine to take on the primary stretch.

modifications.name: Arms Supported on Blocks
modifications.description: Place blocks beside the calves or ankles so the hands rest on them, reducing the sensation for students with very tight hamstrings while maintaining the spinal curve.

modifications.name: Strap Around Feet
modifications.description: Loop a strap around the soles of the feet and hold the ends, allowing a gentle forward pull without collapsing the chest or straining the wrists.

emotional_release_potential.notes: The bladder meridian runs the entire posterior body from the occiput to the little toe; the full back-line stretch can access grief and unexpressed sorrow stored along this channel.
The deeply yielded forward fold activates the kidney meridian and invites the nervous system to release the need for control — existential fear may arise and dissolve.
